title: Exertional heat stroke with DIC: increased thrombin, plasmin, and fibrinolysis
vignette: An 18-year-old woman collapsed while practicing for a marathon in hot, humid weather. The patient subsequently vomited 3 times and had a tonic-clonic seizure. She has no chronic medical conditions and takes no medications. The patient does not use alcohol or illicit drugs. Temperature is 40.8 C (105.4 F), blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg, pulse is 130/min, and respirations are 22/min. The patient is profusely sweating and confused. Pupils are sluggishly reactive to light. Cardiopulmonary examination reveals clear lungs and normal heart sounds. Laboratory results show hemoglobin 15.8 g/dL, platelets 90,000/mm3, leukocytes 10,000/mm3, prothrombin time 20 seconds, and activated partial thromboplastin time 43 seconds. Which of the following sets of hematologic findings is most likely to be present in this patient?

clues.text: collapsed while practicing for a marathon in hot, humid weather
clues.note: Collapse during exertion in the heat with CNS dysfunction is EXERTIONAL HEAT STROKE, which can trigger disseminated intravascular coagulation.
Core temperature 40.8 C (105.4 F) with confusion/seizure = heat stroke; extreme hyperthermia causes tissue injury and release of tissue factor.
Thrombocytopenia (90,000 / normal 150,000-400,000) reflects consumption of platelets in microthrombi - a feature of DIC.

clues.text: prothrombin time 20 seconds, and activated partial thromboplastin time 43 seconds
clues.note: Prolonged PT (20 / normal ~11-15) and aPTT (43 / normal ~25-40) indicate consumption of clotting factors - confirming DIC.

whatMatters: Heat stroke triggered DISSEMINATED INTRAVASCULAR COAGULATION: widespread activation of coagulation (INCREASED THROMBIN, microthrombi) consumes platelets and factors (thrombocytopenia, prolonged PT/PTT), and secondary INCREASED PLASMIN generation and FIBRINOLYSIS clear the clots. All three are increased. Answer E.
strategy: Recognize DIC (thrombocytopenia + prolonged PT/PTT after a trigger) and reason the mechanism: coagulation cascade activation raises THROMBIN (forms microthrombi), which then activates FIBRINOLYSIS via PLASMIN (to clear thrombi, raising D-dimer). So thrombin production up, plasmin generation up, fibrinolysis up. Reject any option with decreased thrombin (coagulation is over-activated) or decreased fibrinolysis/plasmin (secondary fibrinolysis is increased).

options.text: Fibrinolysis decreased, thrombin production decreased, plasmin generation decreased
Fibrinolysis decreased, thrombin production decreased, plasmin generation increased
Fibrinolysis increased, thrombin production decreased, plasmin generation increased
Fibrinolysis increased, thrombin production increased, plasmin generation decreased
Fibrinolysis increased, thrombin production increased, plasmin generation increased
Fibrinolysis decreased, thrombin production increased, plasmin generation decreased

eliminations.label: All decreased - opposite of DIC
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: coagulation and fibrinolysis both suppressed. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: DIC is defined by OVER-activation - increased thrombin generation with reactive increased fibrinolysis; nothing is globally decreased. ✅ Correct if: a state of impaired hemostasis without activation (not DIC).

eliminations.label: Thrombin down, plasmin up - thrombin should be up
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: reduced thrombin but increased plasmin. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: DIC begins with EXCESS thrombin generation (tissue factor activation); thrombin is increased, not decreased. ✅ Correct if: primary hyperfibrinolysis without coagulation activation.

eliminations.label: Thrombin down, fibrinolysis/plasmin up - thrombin wrong
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: decreased thrombin with increased plasmin/fibrinolysis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the driving event in DIC is increased thrombin; the prolonged PT/PTT reflect CONSUMPTION after over-activation, not reduced thrombin generation. ✅ Correct if: isolated primary fibrinolysis.

eliminations.label: Thrombin up, plasmin down - fibrinolysis should rise
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: increased thrombin but decreased plasmin. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: excess thrombin/microthrombi trigger SECONDARY fibrinolysis with increased plasmin (elevated D-dimer); plasmin is increased. ✅ Correct if: thrombosis with suppressed fibrinolysis (not DIC).

eliminations.label: Thrombin up, fibrinolysis/plasmin down - fibrinolysis wrong
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: increased thrombin with decreased fibrinolysis/plasmin. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: DIC's microthrombi activate plasmin-mediated fibrinolysis, so fibrinolysis is INCREASED (D-dimer rises). ✅ Correct if: a purely prothrombotic state without reactive fibrinolysis.

reasoning: Heat stroke causes tissue injury and tissue-factor release, triggering DIC
Coagulation cascade over-activation increases thrombin and forms microthrombi (consuming platelets and factors -> thrombocytopenia, prolonged PT/PTT)
Microthrombi trigger secondary fibrinolysis: plasmin generation and fibrinolysis increase (elevated D-dimer)
-> thrombin, plasmin, and fibrinolysis all increased; answer E
mechanism: EXERTIONAL HEAT STROKE (collapse during exertion in heat with core temp >40 C and CNS dysfunction) causes widespread tissue ischemia/necrosis and release of procoagulant TISSUE FACTOR, which can trigger DISSEMINATED INTRAVASCULAR COAGULATION (DIC). In DIC, the extrinsic (tissue factor) COAGULATION CASCADE is massively activated, generating excess THROMBIN and cross-linked fibrin MICROTHROMBI throughout the microvasculature. This consumes PLATELETS (thrombocytopenia) and clotting FACTORS (prolonging PT and aPTT). Secondary FIBRINOLYSIS is then activated to clear the intravascular thrombi: plasminogen is converted to PLASMIN, which degrades cross-linked fibrin and releases fibrin-degradation products (elevated D-dimer). Thus THROMBIN production, PLASMIN generation, and FIBRINOLYSIS are ALL INCREASED. Clinically DIC produces both bleeding (oozing from puncture sites) and microthrombotic end-organ injury. The correct hematologic set is increased fibrinolysis, increased thrombin production, and increased plasmin generation.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Heme > DIC: triggers (sepsis, trauma, obstetric, malignancy, heat stroke); tissue factor -> increased thrombin -> microthrombi (consume platelets/factors -> thrombocytopenia, prolonged PT/PTT) -> secondary fibrinolysis (increased plasmin, high D-dimer, low fibrinogen).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: DIC = over-activated coagulation (thrombin up) with reactive fibrinolysis (plasmin up, fibrinolysis up).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on DIC, thrombin, plasmin/fibrinolysis, tissue factor, D-dimer, or consumption coagulopathy? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Any 'thrombin decreased' misreads the prolonged PT/PTT (that's CONSUMPTION); fibrinolysis/plasmin are increased, not decreased.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: DIC = increased thrombin + increased plasmin + increased fibrinolysis; consumption -> low platelets, high PT/PTT, high D-dimer, low fibrinogen.

keywords.back: Thrombin up, plasmin up, fibrinolysis up
Low platelets, prolonged PT/PTT, high D-dimer, low fibrinogen
Sepsis, trauma, obstetric, malignancy, heat stroke

firstAid.detail: Heme: increased thrombin + plasmin + fibrinolysis; consumption coagulopathy.
Path > tissue factor release triggers DIC.
Heme > low platelets, high PT/PTT, high D-dimer, low fibrinogen.

memoryHook: DIC is a clotting bonfire: thrombin blazes up making clots (eating platelets and factors), and plasmin rushes in to put them out - everything's turned UP.
